text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Hello. Your sister C has reached out about your father's house and the will. She mentioned you'd like to buy it with your husband at a "family discount", and that B may need money too. Before anything is decided, it would help to hear your side. Would you tell me what you think is fair, and what matters most to you? I'm here to help the three of you reach an agreement together.

I think fairness means accounting for all three of us, but I don’t know what price or shares would be fair. I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, and C’s agreement matters—she hasn’t agreed yet. What matters most to me is having a stable, independent future. I know B wants money, but not why.

Hello. Your sister C has contacted me about your father's house and the will, and I'd like to hear from you as well. She mentioned you could use some money from the estate. Could you share what your situation is and what you think would be fair? I'm here to help all three of you work out a plan together.

I’d like to use my share to start a dance studio, though I’m not sure what would be fair until we’ve discussed the house and the will together. I know A wants to buy the house, and C hasn’t agreed, so perhaps we can talk through everyone’s needs first.

Thank you. That's helpful. To summarise where things stand: you'd like to buy the house with your husband at a price everyone accepts, B wants to fund a dance studio, and C has concerns about any discount that she hasn't agreed to. A common way forward is to agree the house's market value first, then discuss any discount openly, so each sister's share is clear. Would you be open to that? Also, would you be willing to hear more about B's plans before any price is fixed?
Yes, I’m open to establishing the market value and discussing any discount openly, with C’s agreement. I don’t know what B needs the money for, so I’d hear her plans before fixing a price.

Thank you for sharing. B has told me she'd like to use her share to start a dance studio, and she'd also prefer we all discuss the house and will together before deciding anything. A has said she wants to buy the house with her husband at a price all three of you accept. Would you be open to agreeing the house's market value first, and then discussing whether any family discount applies? That way everyone can see clearly what each share would be.

Yes. Let’s establish the market value first, then discuss any discount and what it means for each of our shares. I haven’t agreed to a discount, and I won’t subsidize A’s purchase. We can take the time to discuss it together.

Good news. A and C have both agreed that the first step is to establish the house's market value, and only then discuss whether any family discount applies and what it would mean for each share. A would also like to hear about your dance studio plans before any price is fixed. Could you share a bit about the studio — roughly what you'd need to get started — so we can keep that in view as we talk?
I’d like to start a small dance studio, but I haven’t worked out a reliable figure yet—it would depend on the space and equipment. I can put together a realistic budget once we know more.

An update from B: she'd like to start a small dance studio, and she'll prepare a realistic budget for it once we know more. Next practical step: may I suggest that the three of you agree to a single independent appraisal of the house, paid from the estate and shared with everyone? That gives one trusted market value to work from. Does that work for you?
An independent appraisal shared with all three of us sounds sensible. I’m not sure the estate should pay for it; we’d need to agree on that.

An update: B will prepare a realistic budget for her dance studio once we know more. Next practical step: may I suggest that the three of you agree to a single independent appraisal of the house, paid from the estate and shared with everyone? That gives one trusted market value to work from before any discount is discussed. Does that work for you?
An independent appraisal shared with all of us works for me. I can’t commit the estate to paying for it; we should agree on that together.

An update: A and C have both agreed to a single independent appraisal of the house, shared with all three of you. Neither is sure yet whether the estate should pay for it — that's something the three of you would decide together. Would you also agree to the appraisal? If yes, the remaining question for all three of you is how to pay for it: from the estate, or split between you. Let me know what you prefer.
Yes, I agree to one independent appraisal shared with all three of us. I’d prefer the estate pay for it, if we all think that’s fair.

B has agreed to the independent appraisal too. She'd prefer the estate pay for it, if all three of you agree that's fair. So all three sisters now support one shared appraisal. Could you say whether you'd accept paying for it from the estate? If any of you prefers to split the cost, we can consider that instead.
I’d be willing to have the estate pay, if C agrees too. The cost arrangement should be agreed by all three of us.

B has agreed to the independent appraisal too. She'd prefer the estate pay for it, if all three of you agree that's fair. Could you say whether you'd accept paying for it from the estate? If you or another sister prefers to split the cost between you, we can consider that instead.
Yes, I think it’s fair for the estate to cover the appraisal if all three of us agree. I can’t decide that for the estate alone.

An update: A and C are both willing for the estate to pay for the appraisal, as long as all three of you agree. Do you agree? If yes, the agreed plan is: one independent appraisal of the house, shared with everyone, paid by the estate — then a discussion of any family discount and each sister's share, including your dance studio budget.
Yes, I agree. One independent appraisal shared with all three of us, paid by the estate, sounds fair. Then we can discuss the discount, shares, and my studio budget.

All three of you have now agreed the plan: one independent appraisal of the house, shared with all three sisters, paid by the estate — then a joint discussion of any family discount, each sister's share, and B's dance studio budget. Thank you for your openness. I suggest the next step is for the three of you to commission the appraisal together, so no one feels it was arranged by a single sister.
That sounds sensible, provided C confirms she agrees too. I don’t want to assume on her behalf.
